Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this task changes a multi-wake dogfish target policy. I’ll first read the workspace contract and the skill, then inspect the required rollout keyframes before touching `solver/`.

The contract confirms that the policy file is the only editable solver file, and that CFD must not be run here. I’m now anchoring the visual evidence to the inherited guidance, score, trajectory/force metrics, and optimizer logs; I’ll keep the existing candidate non-empty throughout.

The visual diagnosis is now clear: the seed does propel itself, but it rapidly yaws into a nearly vertical descent along the right side, never enters the developed four-wake corridor around the target, and exits the lower boundary after only 50.1 released time units. The metrics support that reading: only 2.4% progress, a transient 8.61L closest approach followed by 12.12L final distance, exact velocity/acceleration saturation, and very high command effort. I’m checking the policy/state contract and inherited provenance next so the replacement uses only exposed normalized body-frame signals.

The candidate hypothesis is a bounded bearing-PD steering bias applied to the tail’s traveling-bend target, paired with a slower, smaller state-only oscillator so nominal accelerations sit below the hard cap. This directly tests the observed failure: preserve the seed’s demonstrated self-propulsion, but stop the uncorrected turn and exact actuator saturation. I’m recording that hypothesis in the required provenance notes before editing the policy, as the visual-first skill requires.

The policy is now one coherent candidate: a normalized state-only oscillator plus bounded body-frame bearing steering, with all eight active parameters owned by `target_policy_params()`. The visual-first skill also requires a durable evidence lesson, so I’m distilling the sampled seed’s concrete negative result into the shared experience bank without claiming this unevaluated candidate has succeeded.

The first required check exposed a rendered-workspace defect: `README.md` lists the same assigned parent twice, while the validator requires exactly one copied-parent marker. I’m inspecting the validator and will make the minimal metadata repair needed to unblock the mandated check; the policy and evidence files remain intact.

The metadata duplicate is repaired, and the guidance/provenance check now passes. I’m running the remaining two lightweight checks from the mandated runner: first the Julia policy contract/schema probe, then the repository boundary check. No CFD rollout will be launched.

The Julia contract command did not reach the candidate: this shell image has no `julia` on `PATH` and its login profile also references a missing workspace-local SSH directory. I’m locating the preinstalled Julia executable and will rerun the exact probe directly; this is an environment-path issue, not a policy assertion failure.

All three mandated checks now pass: guidance/provenance, Julia policy contract, and solver boundary. I’m doing one final controller-only integration sanity check—no fluid simulation—to verify the new oscillator’s nominal joint angles, velocities, and accelerations stay below the configured envelope before handing off the candidate for EvE’s later CFD evaluation.

The controller-only 300-time-unit sanity run passes with substantial headroom: nominal maxima are about `18.0°/15.4°` joint angle, `141.4°/85.6°` velocity, and `1109°/673°` acceleration—below the `45°`, `260°`, and `1800°` limits. I’m performing the final file/diff audit now; the actual wake outcome remains intentionally unevaluated until EvE runs CFD after this worker exits.

Completed exactly one multi-wake policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): bounded bearing/rate steering with a lower-energy state oscillator.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): visual diagnosis, evidence cross-check, and falsifiable hypothesis.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:21): added an evidence-backed negative lesson about saturated target-blind propulsion.

All mandated checks pass: guidance provenance, Julia contract/schema, and solver boundary. A controller-only 300-unit integration remained within actuator limits. No CFD was run. I also removed a duplicated assigned-parent marker in `README.md` that initially prevented the required validator from identifying one parent.
